fact: 1922年10月24日，墨索里尼在那不勒斯向6万名法西斯民兵发表演说，宣布「我们的纲领很简单：我们要统治意大利」。次日，四巨头（Quadrumviri）德博诺、巴尔博、比安基、德韦基被任命领导向罗马进军，墨索里尼本人前往米兰，并未参加行军，但允许拍摄他随队行进的照片，次日才前往罗马。

sources.title: Wikipedia, March on Rome
sources.quote: On 24 October 1922, Mussolini declared in front of 60,000 militants at a Fascist rally in Naples: "Our program is simple: we want to rule Italy." On the following day, the Quadrumvirs, Emilio De Bono, Italo Balbo, Michele Bianchi and Cesare Maria de Vecchi, were appointed by Mussolini at the head of the march, while he went to Milan. He did not participate in the march, though he allowed pictures to be taken of him marching along with the Fascist marchers, and he went to Rome the next day.

fact: 1922年10月28日，法西斯示威者与黑衫军民兵向首都推进；首相法克塔主张宣布戒严，被国王维托里奥·埃马努埃莱三世否决，国王因惧怕流血而威胁退位，迫使法克塔辞职。10月30日国王任命墨索里尼为首相，政权在未发生武装冲突的情况下转移给法西斯；10月31日黑衫军在罗马游行，墨索里尼组建联合政府。

sources.title: Wikipedia, March on Rome
sources.quote: In late October 1922, Fascist Party leaders planned a march on Rome. On 28 October, the fascist demonstrators and Blackshirt paramilitaries approached the capital; Prime Minister Luigi Facta wished to declare a state of siege, but this was overruled by King Victor Emmanuel III, who, fearing bloodshed, persuaded Facta to resign by threatening to abdicate. On 30 October 1922, the King appointed Mussolini as Prime Minister, thereby transferring political power to the fascists without armed conflict. On 31 October the fascist Blackshirts paraded in Rome, while Mussolini formed his coalition government.

fact: 向罗马进军的队伍不足3万人，但国王部分因为惧怕内战而让步，因为黑衫军已控制波河平原与全国大部分地区，法西斯已不再被视为对现存秩序的威胁。10月29日墨索里尼被要求组阁，当时约2.5万名黑衫军在罗马游行。他依《阿尔贝蒂诺宪章》合法取得政权：这不是法西斯后来宣传的「夺取政权」，而是在宪法框架内的权力移交，由公共当局在法西斯恐吓面前的屈服所促成。许多工商业与金融界领袖相信可以操纵墨索里尼，因为他早期演说与政策强调自由市场与放任主义。

sources.title: Wikipedia, March on Rome
sources.quote: The march itself was composed of fewer than 30,000 men, but the King in part feared a civil war since the squadristi had already taken control of the Po plain and most of the country, while Fascism was no longer seen as a threat to the establishment. Mussolini was asked to form his cabinet on 29 October 1922, while some 25,000 Blackshirts were parading in Rome. Mussolini thus legally reached power, in accordance with the Statuto Albertino, the Italian Constitution. The March on Rome was not the seizure of power which Fascism later celebrated but rather the precipitating force behind a transfer of power within the framework of the constitution. This transition was made possible by the surrender of public authorities in the face of fascist intimidation. Many business and financial leaders believed it would be possible to manipulate Mussolini, whose early speeches and policies emphasized free market and laissez faire economics.

fact: 1922年10月墨索里尼上台时，法西斯在议会中只有35名议员，另有10名民族主义盟友。他处于弱势，依赖与其他政党的联合，联合随时可能瓦解并迫使国王解除其职务。这一议会算术是1923年《阿切尔博法》出台的背景：该法规定得票最多且超过25%的政党获得三分之二席位，1923年7月21日众议院通过、11月14日参议院通过、11月18日国王批准。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Acerbo Law
sources.quote: However, he still only had 35 deputies in Parliament and 10 Nationalist allies. He was in a weak position and relied on the coalition with other parties that could easily unravel and force King Victor Emmanuel III to dismiss him.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Acerbo Law（立法进程栏）
sources.quote: Passed 21 July 1923 ... Passed 14 November 1923 ... Assented to 18 November 1923

fact: 1922年11月19日，意大利政府颁布法令撤销「战争利润委员会」（Commission on war profits）；1923年4月19日的法律把人寿保险移交私营企业，废除1912年设立国家保险局、并预定十年后建立国家垄断的法律；1923年8月20日的法律取消家庭范围内的遗产税。这套「去管制＋减税」的组合是法西斯执政初期对工商业的让利。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Economy of fascist Italy
sources.quote: The 19 April 1923 law transferred life insurance to private enterprise, repealing a 1912 law that created a State Institute for insurances, which had envisioned construction of state monopoly ten years later. Furthermore, a 19 November 1922 decree suppressed the Commission on war profits while the 20 August 1923 law suppressed the inheritance tax inside the family circle.

fact: 法西斯小队（squadristi）在1920—1922年间对社会主义者、工会与合作社发动「惩罚远征」，以暴力摧毁其组织。1921年选举期间发生207起政治谋杀，受害者中社会主义者远多于法西斯分子。墨索里尼1921年8月与意社会党、总工会签订《和解公约》试图约束小队，但被各地头目无视。1922年10月28日向罗马进军后，暴力并未停止。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Squadrismo
sources.quote: During the elections of 1921, the violence continued despite Mussolini's electoral success. There were 207 political killings occurred, and substantially more of the victims were socialists than fascists. Mussolini attempted to reduce the violence by the Pact of Pacification, but it soon became ineffective and was entirely ignored by squadristi. ... The March on Rome on 28 October 1922 further enhanced Mussolini's seizure of power, with thousands of squadristi marching through the Italian capital. King Victor Emmanuel III proceeded to appoint Mussolini to lead the new administration, but that did not stop squadrismo violence

fact: 意大利生活费指数（1914年=100）：1918年7月197，1919年205，1920年313，1921年387，1922年429，1923年487。即1922年的生活成本约为战前的4.3倍。同一来源给出实际工资指数（1914年=100）：建筑业1921年173，纺织业1921年162，机械业1921年154——名义工资的上涨部分抵消了物价，但各行业差异很大。

sources.title: Conze & Wilkinson, Part I: How Fascism Comes（引意大利生活费指数）
Conze & Wilkinson, Part I: How Fascism Comes（引国际劳工局实际工资指数）
sources.quote: The real wages of the Italian workers were according to the Bureau International de Travail: 1914 1919 1920 1921 Building 100 135 126 173 Textile 100 125 111 162 Chemistry 100 – 125 112 Livre 100 84 126 154

fact: 据共产国际1934年引用意大利官方统计，1922年意大利工人平均日工资为18.13里拉；法西斯上台一年后的1923年降至16.92里拉，到1932年降至13.92里拉、1933年13.60里拉。该来源同时指出官方统计只覆盖法西斯工会合同下的减薪，不包括私营业主的变相减薪（解雇后低薪重雇、以女工童工替代等）。

sources.title: The XIII Plenum of the ECCI, Inprecorr（1934-02-05）
sources.quote: Fascism came into power in 1922. The average daily wage was at that time 18.13 lire. In 1923, one year after fascism had come into power, it suddenly dropped to 16.92. ... by 1932 the average daily wage had fallen to 13.92 lire, and in 1933 to 13.60.

fact: 意大利里拉在1922年为90里拉兑1英镑，1925年贬至135里拉兑1英镑。直到1925年意大利经济仅有温和增长，但结构性弱点推高通胀、货币缓慢下跌。墨索里尼任首相的第一年（1922年），意大利国债为930亿里拉；1934年反法西斯历史学家萨尔维米尼估计升至1490亿里拉。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Economy of fascist Italy
sources.quote: Up until 1925, the country enjoyed modest growth, but structural weaknesses increased inflation and the currency slowly fell (Lit.90 to £1 stg in 1922, Lit.135 to £1 stg in 1925). ... In Mussolini's first year as Prime Minister in 1922, Italy's national debt stood at Lit.93 billion.

fact: 皮雷利公司（Pirelli & C.）自1922年起在意大利证券交易所（Borsa Italiana）挂牌上市。该公司1872年由乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·皮雷利在米兰创立，最初专营橡胶及其衍生工艺，此后业务集中于轮胎与能源、通信电缆。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Pirelli
sources.quote: The company, which has been listed on the Borsa Italiana since 1922, is the 5th-largest tyre manufacturer ... Founded in Milan in 1872 by Giovanni Battista Pirelli (1848–1932), the company initially specialised in rubber and derivative processes ... Thereafter, Pirelli's activities were primarily focused on the production of tyre and cables (for energy and telecommunications).

fact: 意大利电影业在1920年代上半期急剧萎缩：产量从1921年的350部降至1924年的60部。原因包括生产组织混乱、成本上升、技术落后、丧失海外市场、无法与好莱坞竞争，以及创作队伍世代更替失败——制片人多为文学出身，无法应对现代性挑战。Cines、Ambrosio等大厂曾组建「意大利电影联合公司」（UCI）协调全国制片战略，但因制片与放映脱节（部分影片拍完数年后才发行）而大体失败。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Cinema of Italy
sources.quote: The first half of the 1920s marked a sharp decrease in production; from 350 films produced in 1921 to 60 in 1924. ... With the end of World War I, Italian cinema went through a period of crisis due to many factors such as production disorganization, increased costs, technological backwardness, loss of foreign markets and inability to cope with international competition, in particular with that of Hollywood. ... Several major studios, among them Cines and Ambrosio, formed the Unione Cinematografica Italiana to coordinate a national strategy for film production. This effort was largely unsuccessful, however, due to a wide disconnect between production and exhibition (some movies weren't released until several years after they were produced).

fact: 米兰的橡胶与电缆工业在1922年已具备出口与上市融资能力：皮雷利以轮胎、能源电缆与通信电缆为主业，1922年在意大利证券交易所上市。该公司在2005年将电缆业务出售给高盛，该部门后更名普睿司曼（Prysmian）；皮雷利本身成为全球第五大轮胎制造商。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Pirelli
sources.quote: In 2005, Pirelli sold its cable division to Goldman Sachs, which changed the new group's name to Prysmian. ... is the 5th-largest tyre manufacturer

fact: 法西斯政府上台后把公共工程作为政权合法性的支柱之一：1922—1942年间为学校建设投入4亿里拉公共资金，而1862—1922年的六十年间仅为6000万里拉。这一支出规模意味着建筑、建材、家具与运输环节在1920年代持续获得政府订单。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Economy of fascist Italy
sources.quote: As for public works, Mussolini's administration "devoted 400 million lire of public monies" for school construction between 1922 and 1942, compared to only 60 million lire between 1862 and 1922.
